title: Almoravids sack Koumbi Saleh
description: Almoravid Berbers from the western Sahara storm the capital of ancient Ghana, by tradition the blow from which the empire never recovers.

title: Nuno Tristão reaches the Bay of Arguin
description: The Portuguese captain pushes past Cape Blanc and into the great bay, where he takes captives to sell in Lagos.

title: Portuguese post at Arguin
description: Prince Henry the Navigator sets up a feitoria on Arguin island, one of the first permanent European posts on the coast of West Africa, trading gum arabic, gold and slaves.

title: Dutch take Arguin
description: The Dutch West India Company seizes the island post, which passes later to Brandenburg and France as the gum trade shifts hands.

title: French territory of Mauritania created
description: Xavier Coppolani's peaceful penetration wins over the Moorish marabouts, and France organises Mauritania as a protectorate run from Saint-Louis.

title: Coppolani killed
description: The architect of the pénétration pacifique is killed by followers of the qadiri leader Shaykh Sidiyya's rivals, and the conquest turns violent.

title: Independence from France
description: Mauritania becomes independent with Moktar Ould Daddah as president, its new capital rising from a village.

title: Iron ore exports begin
description: A 700-kilometre railway carries the first ore from the desert mines to the coast, soon the backbone of the economy.

title: Army overthrows Ould Daddah
description: The bloodless coup of Moustapha Ould Salek ends eighteen years of rule by the party founder, amid a ruinous desert war.

title: Withdrawal from Western Sahara
description: Mauritania makes peace with the Polisario Front and gives up its share of the former Spanish Sahara, which Morocco then occupies entirely.

title: Slavery formally abolished
description: A military decree outlaws slavery, though enforcement will remain the country's great unfinished business for decades.

title: Taya takes power
description: Colonel Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya peacefully deposes Mohamed Khouna Ould Haidalla and rules for twenty-one years.

title: Border war with Senegal
description: A grazing dispute on the river frontier explodes into riots and mass expulsions on both sides, with hundreds of black Mauritanians killed or driven out.

title: Taya wins multiparty election
description: Ould Taya wins the first presidential election under the new constitution amid opposition claims of fraud.

title: Ould Taya overthrown
description: Colonel Ely Ould Mohamed Vall seizes power while Taya is abroad and promises, unusually, to hand over by elections.

title: Abdallahi elected president
description: Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi wins the run-off in the country's first election without an army man on the ballot.

title: Abdel Aziz coup
description: General Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz deposes Abdallahi after the president tries to dismiss him and the other service chiefs.

title: Abdel Aziz elected
description: The coup leader legitimises his rule by winning the presidential election in the first round.

title: Ghazouani elected president
description: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani wins the run-off, the first peaceful transfer between elected presidents in Mauritania's history.
